description: Answer the question that decides whether `make` is giving you anything: is this Makefile a BUILD, or a script LAUNCHER? make exists in order NOT to redo what is already done — mtimes, a dependency graph, skipping what did not change — and most Makefiles today use none of it: they are `make test`, `make lint`, `make docker-up`, all .PHONY, all running every time. Here each target is classified WITH THE SIGNAL that decided it (including the signals that pointed the other way: a .PHONY whose recipe creates that very file is a bug waiting to happen), what make is giving you TODAY is measured, and with `convertTo` it is converted to just, Taskfile or npm scripts. Whatever cannot be converted is OMITTED with its reason, rather than emitting a recipe that would look the same and rebuild every time. Honest caveat: `make` is POSIX and is everywhere; just and task have to be installed.

convertTo.description: If given, also convert to that format instead of only diagnosing
